claim: GHSA-9493-h29p-rfm2 / CVE-2025-31133 (published 2025-11-05): runc container escape via masked-path abuse and mount races (/dev/null replaced by a symlink lets runc bind-mount a host path; deleting /dev/null silently skips maskedPaths); affects runc <=1.2.7, 1.3.0-rc.1..1.3.2, 1.4.0-rc.1..rc.2; fixed 1.2.8, 1.3.3, 1.4.0-rc.3; 'runc 1.1.x and earlier are no longer supported and thus have not been patched'

Wiz NVIDIAScape CVE-2025-23266 (CVSS 9.0): NVIDIA Container Toolkit createContainer hook runs with host privileges and inherits container env vars, so LD_PRELOAD in an image gives host root; affects toolkit <=1.17.7 and GPU Operator <=25.3.x; second toolkit escape after CVE-2024-0132 [source: security researcher]

Kubernetes Pod Security Standards: Baseline 'prevents known privilege escalations' and disallows hostNetwork/hostPID/hostIPC, privileged containers ('disable most security mechanisms') and hostPath volumes; the Privileged profile 'allows for known privilege escalations'

systemd-sysext man page: default --image-policy for sysexts is 'root=verity+signed+encrypted+unprotected+absent:usr=verity+signed+encrypted+unprotected+absent' (confext 'root=verity+signed+encrypted+unprotected+absent'), i.e. unsigned images are accepted by default; only /.extra/sysext/ in the initrd defaults to signed; directories in the search paths are accepted as directory-based extension images

kairos-io/kairos issue #4988 (opened 2026-09-26, closed 2026-09-29): immucore validated sysext images against the signed image policy only on the UKI path and linked every *.raw unchecked on GRUB; because 'systemd-sysext refresh' is all-or-nothing, one non-compliant image stopped every extension from merging; first fix failed on real GRUB boot because systemd-dissect was missing from the initramfs and immucore fell back to enabling everything unvalidated

systemd PR #44234 (opened 2026-10-16, merged 2026-10-26 to main as e472d3e): verity signature checks now depend on host image policy, not image contents ('The image is input we don't trust'); closes two bypasses under a signature-requiring policy: reuse of a shared verity device set up without a validated signature, and direct partition mount when no root hash is known; release containing it not stated

Linux kernel module-signing docs: the public key is built into the kernel; the private key 'must be either destroyed or moved to a secure location' because 'viruses and malware could use the private key to sign modules'; without CONFIG_MODULE_SIG_FORCE unsigned modules load and only taint; the page describes no revocation mechanism

TUF security model: defines indefinite freeze attacks (client kept on files it has already seen), rollback attacks (older files presented), single-key compromise, and recommends a threshold/quorum of signatures for compromise resilience

ReversingLabs (reported by Techworm 2025-08-30): VS Code Marketplace frees the name of a removed extension for anyone to reuse (unpublished names stay reserved); malicious 'shiba' extensions were republished under a reused name weeks after removal; no Microsoft fix announced at the time

Datadog (reported by Help Net Security 2025-05-21): three malicious Solidity-tool extensions (Solaibot, among-eth, blankebesxstnion) on the official VS Code Marketplace installed a credential stealer; removed after <50 downloads; the actor kept editing intermediate payloads after removal

Trend Micro (2025-11-27): Shai-Hulud 2.0 used stolen maintainer npm tokens to republish up to 100 of the victim's packages at once with a preinstall payload (setup_bun.js), bumped patch versions, registered a persistent self-hosted GitHub Actions runner and injected a workflow exfiltrating repository secrets [source: security researcher]
